### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **5** documentable anchor(s).

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/deployment/validating-metadata.mdx`  _(via AUTHORING_RULES (symbol, a top-level const object))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **172** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6e1ab9b286655c5476312ae563ab531f3f36cf38` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `d6c1cf20d4112e29732a134f1516f35025bf7d15` — the merge of head `9d07ffa069baf93055b4da43e19fccbf9237159c` into base `6e1ab9b286655c5476312ae563ab531f3f36cf38`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin d6c1cf20d4112e29732a134f1516f35025bf7d15 && git checkout d6c1cf20d4112e29732a134f1516f35025bf7d15
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 6e1ab9b286655c5476312ae563ab531f3f36cf38 9d07ffa069baf93055b4da43e19fccbf9237159c && git checkout -B drift-repro 6e1ab9b286655c5476312ae563ab531f3f36cf38 && git merge --no-ff 9d07ffa069baf93055b4da43e19fccbf9237159c

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6e1ab9b286655c5476312ae563ab531f3f36cf38
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 6e1ab9b286655c5476312ae563ab531f3f36cf38` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `15d074782c704e5b016436ec2ac8102d5d18411c`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.object-extension-validation-rule-expression-judged.ts + packages/lint/src/validate-expressions.ts, packages/lint/src/authoring-rules.ts, packages/lint/src/runtime-gate.object-formula-writes.test.ts, packages/lint/src/authored-site-expression.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/meta-object-extension-item.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/packages-disable-module-extension-fields.test.ts

PR #33205 for card #33154, on the schema face (the semantic entry) and the declared narrowing. Read: the card body and its five comments (6865785642, 6868572380, 6868654518, 6869487624, 6870691534), the PR body and its nine-path file list, the net diff against `main`, and the head's check-runs at 2026-11-14T03:27Z: 68 runs, 58 success, 10 skipped, none failed or pending, the last completed 2026-11-14T03:05Z. Every statement about behaviour below is read from the tree at the head. Nothing was built or run.

**One must-fix (F1), one should-fix (F2), three nits (N1 to N3).**

### ① Derived judgments

1. **`os build`, `os validate` and `os lint` refuse a stack whose `objectExtensions[].validations[]` rule fails the rule pass.** Right, and a narrowing. The rule's registry entry is `commands: ALL` (`authoring-rules.ts:648`), so `os lint` is a third CLI door. The changeset and the entry name the first two only.
2. **The runtime `object_extension` publish door refuses the same rule with `422 INVALID_METADATA`, issue `expression-invalid`.** Right as declared, except that the door also refuses one shape the declaration does not cover (F1).
3. **The newly refused shapes.** An unknown field, a bare reference, an unregistered function, an unguarded nullable ordering or arithmetic operand, a `parent` root, a type mismatch, and the hop shapes a declared rule is refused for. Each is a verdict the object's own rules already get. The changeset spells four of them and covers the rest by "the same rule on the object". Right. One refused shape is not named, and is wrong: F1. One declared judgment is not delivered: F2.
4. **No exported type or signature moves in `@objectstack/lint`.** Right. `judgeValidationRule` is a closure inside `runStackExpressionPasses`, and `StackExpressionOptions` changes in its docblock only.
5. **`@objectstack/spec` gains one semantic entry in the protocol 18 step**, so `os migrate meta` prints one more block. Right, additive.
6. **A new locator.** `object 'T' · ENTRY · validation 'N'` (nested: `validation rule 'N' then → 'M'`), key path `ENTRY.validations[k].SLOT`, under the object's own rule id. Right.
7. **The object walk is unchanged.** Right. Compared line by line, the hoisted body differs from the inline one on `main` in three places, each `object '${objectName}'` becoming `${locus}`, and the object call site passes `locus` as that same string.
8. **Not gated, as before:** a module package registered at boot, and the package-wide draft publish limit the options docblock already states. As declared.

### ② Semver level

The changeset moves `@objectstack/lint` and `@objectstack/spec` at `minor`. Both are released packages the diff moves (lint source, one spec migration entry), and the kind `narrowed` takes at least `minor`, so the level is right. `packages/runtime` changes in tests only and publishes nothing, so it owes no entry.

The `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` line and `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` stand line-initial on the PR body and on the changeset body. The changeset carries the BREAKING banner, the fix, and exactly one ADR-0087 marker, `registered object-extension-validation-rule-expression-judged`, which is the entry's id. `Check Changeset` and `Lint · CI, release & engine gates` are green on the head. The arm is the right arm. The bound it states, "a `condition` or `when` the same rule on the object itself is refused for", is exceeded at the door (F1).

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Dev report `open_questions`:** empty.
- **Dev report `deviations`:** the attribution line links the card thread, and the ablation's mutate leg needed `--source-marker`. Neither touches the contract. Accepted.
- **Dev report out-of-scope finding** (a `format` rule's regex and a `json_schema` rule's formats in an extension's `validations` are judged at neither door): confirmed by reading. Both rules walk `obj.validations` only (`validate-rule-compilability.ts:429`). It is a trap of this card's own class, so a card is owed. **Escalated to seat 2**, the carrier the report names. The changeset's Unchanged line states it.
- **The claim's provisional `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`:** stands.
- **Amendment 6868654518** (comment only in `authoring-rules.ts`): held. Seven comment lines; `runtimeTypes` and the adapter are untouched.
- **Amendment 6869487624** (the repaired fixture; the banner and the entry must name the null-guard refusal and its fix): held. Both name it, with the guard.
- **File surface:** the nine paths are the claimed surface plus the two amendments. No breach.
- **New from this review, escalated to seat 2:** F2 needs a follow-up card. The flow and hook passes read the same nullable index at their own doors (`validate-expressions.ts:3045`, `:4255`). That is outside this diff and not measured; if F1's measurement confirms the served form there, it is a card too.

### ④ Design judgment

What was tried against the design, and held:

- **A rule reading a field another extension adds.** It resolves at the build through `fieldIndex` over `objectsAsServed`, and at the door through the live target. `packages-disable-module-extension-fields.test.ts` is a real-door instance: the tenant pair's rule reads `qx_credit`, which the module's extension adds.
- **A republish judged without the package's stored self.** `objectExtensionWriteFold` takes the written package's extension off the target, and the republish case pins it: dropping `bonus__c` while the rule still reads it is refused.
- **The one-pass rule.** The object walk and the flow walk read an empty list on an extension write, and the function returns at `validate-expressions.ts:4136`. Pinned by the case where the target's own broken rule is not charged to the extension write.
- **Rule id and locator.** `expression-invalid`, located at the entry, pinned at both doors.
- **Tracker ids in printed guidance.** None (see the entry below).

**`packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.object-extension-validation-rule-expression-judged.ts`** (`hits`)

- The four printed fields, `surface`, `replacement`, `reason` and `acceptanceCriteria`, hold no `#` followed by digits. The one id sits in the leading comment, which is not printed. That is the line `packages/cli/test/migrate-meta-engine-guidance.test.ts` holds every entry to.
- No D2 conversion and no `relevantWhen`: both right. The repair is a fact only the author holds, and the surface also lives in stored `object_extension` rows a stack does not show.
- Its premise holds against the registry: `mergeValidationsByName` (`packages/objectql/src/registry.ts:1160`) merges an extension's rules onto the target by name.
- It does not hold against the door for one input: its `replacement` (lines 23 to 28) and `acceptanceCriteria` (lines 38 to 41) are false there. See F1.
- N3 below.

**`packages/lint/src/validate-expressions.ts`** (implementing)

The hoist is faithful (① item 7). The extension loop passes the target, the entry locator and the rule's key path, and the return after the walk is intact. Two findings on the contract, two nits.

**F1, must-fix. At the real `object_extension` door the null-guard gate reads the registry's injected system columns as nullable declared fields, so the door refuses a rule that `os build` and the object's own rule pass accept.**

- **Mechanism.** The door hands the walk its live objects: `registry.listItems('object')` folded with the stored rows (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-authoring-gate.ts:437-474`). A registered base layer carries its injected columns in `fields`, because `applySystemFields` runs before contributor storage (`packages/objectql/src/registry.ts:5890-5895`). Each is defined `required: false` with no `defaultValue` (`packages/spec/src/data/injected-system-column-provenance.ts:61-97`). Nothing between the registry and the walk strips them. `nullableIndex` is built from those objects (`validate-expressions.ts:2379`, `isNullableField` at `:493`), and the new loop sends each extension rule through `checkNullGuards` for the target (`:3641`, `:4126`).
- **Effect.** An extension rule with an unguarded ordering or arithmetic operand over `record.created_at` or `record.updated_at` (or any other injected column) is refused 422 at the door.
  - `os build` accepts the same entry, because the declared target carries no injected column. The index's own docblock (`:508`) says it holds declared fields only, so that a `record.created_at` comparison does not become an error.
  - The object save door accepts the same rule declared on the object, because its subject is the body stripped at `protocol-save.ts:582`.
- **The tree already states this.** `packages/lint/src/authored-site-expression.ts:105-111` strips the injected columns off registry-served definitions before this same pass, and says why: unstripped, the null-guard gate would judge `created_at` as a declared nullable field. The extension door does not strip. One consequence is that the MCP `validate_expression` tool answers clean for a rule the extension publish then refuses.
- **Why it is a contract fault.** On an update the stored row always holds `created_at` (the index's docblock: the driver always populates it), so for a rule that runs on update the refusal is false. Whether the column is already bound when an insert rule runs was not traced; if it is not, the door is right there and the build under-covers. Either way the door and the build disagree, and three shipped sentences are false for this input:
  - the entry's `replacement` ("A rule the expression rule accepts on a declared rule of the same object") and its `acceptanceCriteria` (a clean `os build`, then a 200);
  - the declared bound on the changeset and the PR body;
  - the docs sentence "at the door and in `os build` alike".
- **Why the pins do not see it.** The lint PARITY case gives the door an authored-shaped target, and the three real-door cases read `name`, `nmae` and a field the extension adds. The type index (`:2378`) has the same served-form difference, there in the truthful direction.
- **Basis.** Read, not run. One real-door case settles it: an extension rule with an unguarded ordering operand over `record.created_at`, published through `saveMetaItem` and `publishMetaItem`, beside `os build` of the same entry.
- **Remedy, the dev's choice.** Either judge the door's objects as authored on an extension write (the strip `judgeAuthoredSiteExpression` uses), so the door gives the build's verdict; or keep the door's verdict and name it in the entry, the changeset and the docs sentence. Either way, pin it at the real door.

**F2, should-fix. A one-hop read through a reference field an extension adds has its leaf unjudged, so the card's trap stays open in that corner.**

- `refuseUndeclaredHopField` (`:2447`, the loop at `:2458`) and `storedMetadataBodyReferencesFor` (`:2386`) read the reference field's definition off the declared `objects`, not off the served fold.
- So an extension that adds a lookup, and a rule that reads a misspelt column through it and is otherwise well formed, is accepted at the build. At the door it is accepted when the lookup is the written entry's own. By the helper's own docblock, such a rule then "has no verdict and refuses every write it judges".
- The helper predates this PR and a formula has the same gap. But the new comment at `:4111-4114` and the changeset say the rule is judged "against the target as served, through the same indexes", which is wider than what is enforced. A lookup and a rule in one extension is the natural shape on this surface.
- Remedy without moving a reviewed file: add this to the changeset's Unchanged line, and file a follow-up card. No case pins it today.

**N1, nit.** The key path's index is a counter over `recordsOf(ext.validations)` (`:4123-4129`, `object-graph.ts:451`). On input `ObjectExtensionSchema` refuses, the path is wrong: a non-record member ahead of the rule shifts the index, and a map-form `validations` gets an index where the object walk spells no path. This is reachable only on an unparsed stack (`os lint`). The locator and the verdict are unaffected. Accepted deviation or a follow-up.

**N2, nit.** The comment at `:4116-4118` says the door re-spells the path item-relative (`validations.0.condition`). The door's 422 keeps `objectExtensions[0].validations[0].condition`, as this PR's own real-door case pins. The item-relative spelling is `itemRelativeIssuePath`'s, where a draft read reports the publish verdict. The hoisted docblock at `:3576-3580` says it correctly.

**N3, nit, in the `hits` file.** Two loose sentences in the entry's `reason`:

- It locates the finding at `objectExtensions[0]` for the build and the door alike. The build locates at the entry's own index, under `packages[J].manifest.` in an artifact, as the lint sibling case pins. `acceptanceCriteria` already spells `[N]`.
- "a rule reading a nullable field with no guard aborted" is wider than the gate, which judges ordering and arithmetic operands only. An equality read is accepted: `record.region__c == null` is this PR's own repaired fixture.

Fix both with F1's edit to the entry, or leave them as accepted deviations.

**`packages/lint/src/authoring-rules.ts`** (implementing)

Comment only, as amended. Its measured sentence holds on reading: `examples/app-showcase` ships one entry with three plain fields, `plugin-auth` one entry with fields only, and neither carries a rule.

**The four test files** (implementing)

- `runtime-gate.object-formula-writes.test.ts`: the eight cases assert what the PR body says. Two blind spots: no door case over a registry-shaped target (F1), and no hop through a reference the extension adds (F2).
- `authored-site-expression.test.ts`: the regions follow the hoist. `indexOf` and `isArray` stay in the object loop, outside the rule pass, so they rightly leave the table.
- `meta-object-extension-item.test.ts`: three real-door cases, and the bare `region__c` fixture repaired to `record.region__c`.
- `packages-disable-module-extension-fields.test.ts`: the tenant rule guarded, as the amendment says.

Outside the diff, read only: the `object_extension` row comment in `packages/lint/src/runtime-gate.ts:293-296` still describes the crossing as the extension walk over the written entry's fields. A follow-up.
